+/// This is a copy of `grep_regex::Matcher::replace_with_captures_at` but with
+/// a modification to support our multi-line look-around kludge. In particular,
+/// it takes a `range` and will not find replacements for matches that start at
+/// or after `range.end`.
+fn replace_with_captures_at_kludge<M: Matcher>(
+    matcher: &M,
+    haystack: &[u8],
+    range: &std::ops::Range<usize>,
+    caps: &mut M::Captures,
+    dst: &mut Vec<u8>,
+    mut matched: impl FnMut(&M::Captures, &mut Vec<u8>) -> bool,
+) -> io::Result<()> {
+    let mut last_match = range.start;
+    matcher
+        .find_iter_at(haystack, range.start, |m| {
+            if m.start() >= range.end {
+                return false;
+            }
+            // Infallible because we got `m` from the same matcher.
+            matcher.captures_at(haystack, caps, m.start()).unwrap();
+
+            dst.extend_from_slice(&haystack[last_match..m.start()]);
+            if !matched(caps, dst) {
+                return false;
+            }
+            last_match = m.end();
+            true
+        })
+        .map_err(io::Error::error_message)?;
+    // The normal `replace_with_captures_at` routine writes through to the
+    // end of haystack, but our kludge demands that we only write through to
+    // the end of the original match that we're rediscovering.
+    //
+    // It is VERY important that we do not write any bytes from `haystack`
+    // beyond `range.end`. That is the entire point of this routine.
+    dst.extend_from_slice(&haystack[last_match..range.end]);
+    Ok(())
+}
